note: Literature on biallelic NOTCH3-related small vessel disease demonstrates that heterozygous carriers of loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic and lack typical CADASIL features.

evidence.text: A comprehensive study on biallelic NOTCH3 disorders observed that heterozygous monoallelic carriers of loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic, lacking early-onset ischemic stroke or dementia and only occasionally reporting nonspecific headaches.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Notably, monoallelic carriers of loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic, with only a few cases reporting nonspecific headaches.

evidence.text: Family segregation analysis revealed that relatives carrying only a frameshift loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant (p.Cys1024Valfs248) showed milder clinical and imaging manifestations compared to carriers of classic cysteine-altering CADASIL mutations.

source.title: An in trans NOTCH3 loss-of-function variant modifies disease severity in CADASIL: A family-based study
source.quote: In contrast, the father (carrying p.Cys1146Ser alone) and the mother and brother (carrying p.Cys1024Valfs248 alone) exhibited milder clinical and imaging phenotypes.
